chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far, from Wahb, from Ja'far, from his father, (peace be upon him), that Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a sheep that died, and milk was drawn from it, so he said:
Ali (peace be upon him): That is pure haram (forbidden).

Therefore, this is a rare (shadh) narration, and its narrator is Wahb ibn Wahb, who is weak as we have clarified previously. And accepting the report, it can be understood as a form of taqiyya (dissimulation), because it is the belief of some of the Sunnis.

key_terms.الْعَامَّةِ: The general public (often referring to Sunni Muslims)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on milk from an animal after it dies?
ai.summary: Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that milk drawn from a sheep after its death is pure haram (forbidden). The scholar notes this is a rare narration from a weak narrator, Wahb ibn Wahb, and suggests it may reflect taqiyya, aligning with the view of some Sunni scholars.
